title: Hosted API nudge messaging for developer trials and metering
body:
Purpose
---
Quick set of microcopy, nudge experiments, and price-framing snippets aimed at increasing trial-to-paid conversion for developer signups on Hosted API. This doc is intentionally lightweight — meant for A/B wiring into the activation flow, billing emails, and in-console banners.

Audience
---
- Primary: individual engineers and small engineering teams trying Redwood Hosted API (free credits)
- Secondary: growth/product managers who own onramp funnels

Success metrics (what we want to move)
---
- Trial activation -> 1st API call within 5 minutes (activation rate)
- Trial-to-paid conversion within 30 days
- Average tokens/month on first paid invoice (monetization velocity)

Constraints and guardrails
---
- Keep messaging developer-technical and pragmatic (no marketing fluff)
- Avoid surprise billing language; emphasize control and transparency
- Short snippets only (5–25 words) for UI; longer explanations for emails/docs

Core developer-first hooks (single-line)
---
- "Start generating in minutes — free credits included."
- "Same API you’ll ship with; swap models without code changes."
- "Predictable latency and clear token billing — no hidden surprises."
- "Try the runtime tuned for production scale — test with real traffic."

Microcopy buckets and examples
---
1) Signup confirmation / welcome email subject + preview
   - Subject: "Your Redwood Hosted API credits are ready"
   - Preview: "Get a quick example and a 1-click curl to call in 30s"

2) Console onboarding banner (short)
   - Banner top-line: "Free credits: 100k tokens — use them to prototype and measure cost."
   - CTA: "Run your first call" (secondary: "See cost estimate")

3) In-product inline nudge (after first successful call fails latency/SLO)
   - "That was fast — want consistent latency? Try Dedicated for predictable throughput."
   - Action: link to comparison modal with estimated marginal cost

4) Pricing/metering microcopy (billing modal)
   - Header: "Transparent token billing"
   - Subline: "Per-token + model multiplier. Estimated cost shown before you run."
   - Tooltip copy: "Model multiplier reflects compute intensity (fewer tokens ≠ cheaper)."

Onramp quickstart scripts (30s / 5 min)
---
- 30s (for demo flows and videos):
  "curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' -d '{\"prompt\":\"Summarize this file in 3 bullets\"}'"
  UI prompt label: "Try a single curl — see a response in under a second"

- 5 min (for docs + email walkthrough):
  1) Create an API key
  2) Run the sample curl
  3) Toggle streaming to see token-level latency
  4) Check the cost-estimate panel and pin a model to test with larger input

Pricing-language experiments (A/B candidates)
---
Variant A (cost transparency focused)
- Headline: "Know your cost before you run"
- Body: "Live cost estimator shows token and model impact. Pause or pin models any time."
- CTA: "Estimate before you run"

Variant B (time-to-value focused)
- Headline: "From zero to working prototype in minutes"
- Body: "Free credits + one-click code samples — integrate and measure unit economics fast."
- CTA: "Start with credits"

Variant C (ops reassurance)
- Headline: "Ship with an inference runtime built for production"
- Body: "SLO-backed latency tiers and predictable pricing for growth stages."
- CTA: "Compare tiers"

Nudge sequences (for emails / in-app flows)
---
- Day 0: Welcome email with 100k credit notice + 30s curl snippet
- Day 1: If no call made — email: "Try this 1-liner — takes 30s" + cost preview image
- Day 3: If calls made but <10k tokens — in-console overlay: "Scale safely: simulate 10k tokens of traffic — see cost estimate"
- Day 7: If active but no payment method — email: "Keep your model live — add a billing method to avoid interruptions" (include cost anchors from example workloads)

Cost anchors (examples to use in copy)
---
- "Simple summarizer: ~0.002 USD per 1k tokens" (use as conservative anchor)
- "Chat-like assistant at 512 tokens/request: ~0.015–0.06 USD per 1k tokens depending on model"
- Include small visual: "Run 1k requests/day => monthly estimate shown in billing modal" (longer explainer on billing page)

Competitive angles and rebuttals (short lines for banners/FAQs)
---
- Competitor claim: "Cheaper per-token models"
  Rebuttal: "We surface model multipliers and performance profiles so you can pick the best cost/latency trade-off for your workload."
- Competitor claim: "Simple API but different runtime in prod"
  Rebuttal: "Same API across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private — no code swap when you scale."
- Competitor claim: "Hidden autoscaling costs"
  Rebuttal: "Transparent reserved vs. burst pricing and a cost estimator to avoid surprises."

Copy tests and telemetry hooks (what to track)
---
- Clicks on CTA (run-first-call / add-billing)
- % of users who view cost estimator before first call
- Time from signup -> first paid invoice
- Lift in average tokens on first paid invoice by experiment cohort

Implementation notes (engineering/experiment wiring)
---
- Place interchangeable copy tokens in onboarding microcopy service (keyed by experiment id)
- Ensure cost estimator is available in the console and exposed via ephemeral preview link for emails
- Add telemetry events: estimator_viewed, estimator_used, first_call_time, billing_added_time

Open questions / tradeoffs
---
- How conservative should the cost anchors be? (users hate surprises, but under-quoting may deter experimentation)
- Do we surface per-request cost in the flow, or only model-level per-1k-token anchors?
- Which trial size performs best — larger credits encourage exploration but reduce urgency to add billing?

Next steps (owner: Aisha)
---
- Iterate 3 copy variants for banner/email and hand to growth for a 4-week A/B test (due: 2025-03-15)
- Ship estimator preview link for emails (eng ticket: GO-612)
- Draft FAQ snippets for billing page and competitor FAQ (owner: Jonas)

Notes to self / rough ideas
---
- Consider a "simulate 1k requests" button that runs in a sandbox and shows cost and latency histogram — high impact for devs doing realistic checks
- Add a small badge on projects showing "estimated monthly cost" based on project activity to reduce billing surprise

End of doc
